# Results (auto-generated by experiments.py)

seeds=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4], lambda=100 CNY/tCO2, grid limit=26.0 MW

Savings are shown only when every run of both methods is feasible. Blank gains mean ineligible, not zero savings. Penalized objectives quantify service loss and overflow; feasibility takes precedence. See run_metrics.csv for individual outcomes and feasibility.csv for worst-case diagnostics. Paired 95% Student-t intervals use within-seed savings (baseline minus method), with n-1 degrees of freedom; percentage intervals estimate the mean per-seed percentage, not the ratio of mean costs. With only three/five synthetic seeds these are approximate, pointwise intervals, not real-site guarantees or simultaneous significance tests. Infeasible pairs are retained and disqualify the whole comparison.

## 10. Illustrative battery investment and demand billing

ASSUMPTIONS, not vendor quotes or applicable tariffs: installed energy costs [500.0, 1000.0, 1500.0] CNY/kWh; power adder 0.0 CNY/kW; life 10 years; discount 8.0%; fixed O&M 1.5% of capex/year; demand rates [0.0, 20.0, 40.0] CNY/kW/month. Annualization repeats each synthetic block to 8760 hours. Its peak is only a monthly-peak proxy, not a measured yearly peak.

Capacity and measured-peak billing are alternatives, never added together. Capital recovery and fixed maintenance are included; throughput degradation is already in operating cost. Battery value is incremental to zero-battery MPC job shifting, not the no-scheduling baseline. NPV excludes carbon credits, tax, subsidy and salvage. Dispatch still optimizes the original energy/carbon objective: these are post-dispatch economic screens, not a demand-charge-optimal dispatch or bankable investment recommendation. Only all-seed feasible cases receive economic rankings. An uncapped contract has no defined capacity charge at a positive rate. Best means best among tested feasible caps only.
